title: The Case for Greenland
summary: Revived 2021 draft arguing Greenland's value rises with Chinese/Indian coal-driven warming: rare earths, Arctic sea lanes, airspace, and a post-globalism strategic rationale, ending on a 'fair market price' deal. Bolts a Greenland-acquisition case onto a China-emissions model.
best_line: Trump’s signature move is to speak with chaos, to force separating equilibria of revealed preferences.
improve: The Evergrande/Greenland Holdings double entendre and the carbon model are a different post than the geopolitical case; split them or drop the 2021 framing.
Reserve and emissions claims (36mt REE, 1,000 GtC budget, 2030 China-passes-US cumulative) are asserted with a one-line source ('Claude and GPT arguing'); cite primary data.
falsifiable_calls: Cumulative Chinese CO2 emissions surpass the US around 2030
Summer Arctic sea ice largely gone by 2040-2050
Greenland settles at a 'fair market price' deal rather than force
return_reason: Greenland negotiation and Arctic/rare-earth angle is live geopolitics worth a follow-up on what actually moved.

title: Silver Moon
summary: Bullish update with silver ~$103: Chinese capital flight, Shanghai premium, COMEX inventory drain, solar/AI demand; lays out tells and the actual trade structure while admitting solar-margin and substitution risks. Published near the top.
best_line: Watch the flows, not the price.
improve: Conclusion 'silver at $103 isn't the end, might not be the middle' is stated with more conviction than the risks section supports; the $134 solar breakeven only 30% away deserved to drive sizing language.
Written 'in a few hours'; headline stats (supply ~1bn oz, Shanghai $114 vs $103) lack sources and the post ends with 'to the moon' just before a crash.
falsifiable_calls: COMEX silver inventories historically low by July and functionally exhausted by September
A central bank will announce a strategic silver reserve
Shanghai premium persisting signals structural demand
return_reason: Silver peaked days later; the flow-based framework and Shanghai premium thesis should be re-tested against what followed.

title: Dollar Doomers Missing the Point
summary: Argues gold/silver bulls need not be dollar bears: reserve currency means ubiquity not strength, the real 'sell America' mechanism is foreigners dumping US stocks and bonds, and the author is long dollars as a hedge on metals. Offers 'double dollar gold' construction.
best_line: The noise is loud but the flows are quiet.
improve: The 'double dollar gold' backtest (higher Sharpe, lower drawdowns) is asserted without showing numbers or period; show the chart.
The 'what would worry me' list (SWIFT share <40%, Japanese life insurers) is the best part and is buried near the end; lead with it.
falsifiable_calls: Dollar decline is a correction not a crisis until DXY approaches 85
Doom shows up first as selling of SPY/TLT/mega-cap tech by foreigners, not DXY futures
Watch Japanese life insurers, SWIFT share, stablecoin flows as confirmation signals
return_reason: The falsifiable watch-list (flows, SWIFT share, insurers) can be checked against subsequent data.

title: When You Feel Pain, Remember to Reflect
summary: Post-mortem of the silver/gold washout: candid emotional reflection, then a mechanistic explanation (short gamma from options dealers, margin leverage, AGQ rebalancing) and the author's own execution mistakes.
best_line: It’s hard to be reflective when you are up 130% on the year.
improve: The 'responsibility to readers' section is rambling and delays the explanation; tighten the first third.
The 6-sigma and 275-year charts carry the claim but several attributions (China selling gold, Warsh as cause) are speculative; separate what is known from narrative.
falsifiable_calls: AGQ-driven selling is behind us and any bounce will force it to buy back
China does not sell all the way off Sunday night
Agents mostly come online in enterprise late Q2, leaving US stocks vulnerable

title: Dear Comrade Xi
summary: Frames what China would have to do to make the RMB a reserve currency (open the capital account both ways, let foreigners fix and short banks, move to title-transfer repo) and argues each step is politically impossible; hence long gold in China, short RMB.
best_line: Being a reserve currency requires humility.
improve: Several claims ($2tn errors and omissions, $5-10tn hidden losses, Tether $200B) are cited from memory without sources or charts.
The close is a plug for 'my book' and a one-line trade; state the short-RMB expression, horizon, and what would invalidate it.
falsifiable_calls: The RMB does not become a reserve currency because Beijing will not take the five steps
Long gold in China, short RMB
return_reason: Pledge repo vs title transfer and the 'minimum viable work' criterion are original and deserve a deeper standalone piece.

title: The Air Pocket
summary: Explains why an AI bull is bearish on stocks near term: capex outruns revenue because agent-driven inference demand lags builds, buybacks give way to debt issuance; and software eating the service economy is now being eaten by agents. Appendix gives a token/FLOP breakeven framework.
best_line: Software didn’t really eat American manufacturing—China did that.
improve: Internal inconsistency: body cites 7% inference utilization while the appendix says use 30% and calls the 70% number irreconcilable; reconcile or drop the 7%.
The moltbook/agents anecdote section is long and tangential to the capex-gap thesis; the appendix math (stale Q4 2024) should be the centerpiece with live inputs.
falsifiable_calls: Utilization climbing toward 40-50% by end of 2026 (bull) vs stuck below 30% (bear); 'check back in 18 months'
Enterprise pricing holding above $0.002 per 1k tokens
Memory prices staying elevated is real demand, not hoarding
return_reason: The author set an explicit 18-month check-back with bullish/bearish indicators; worth scheduling that scorecard.

title: Flash Crash
summary: Real-time tweet-collage on a 17% Shanghai silver drop with gold flat: reads it as a forced liquidation by a large Chinese holder rather than a US 'attack', and describes tactical repositioning.
best_line: Sometimes it pays to be the first call when someone sees something weird. Funny form of alpha.
improve: Tweet pasting leaves the argument fragmentary; one paragraph summarizing the evidence (SHFE vs COMEX normalized, premium compression) would help.
Reads as a diary; note that the attribution was later revised in The Silver Attack.
falsifiable_calls: Silver rallies a bit and gold sells off after the flush
Short-term vol bearish, long-term backdrop bullish for metals

title: The Silver Attack
summary: Free sample of paid content: tracks a large Shanghai silver short (Bian Ximing, ~30,000 lots, >100% of warehouse stocks), now barred from adding or rolling, as a trapped seller; yet stays flat because risk-off liquidation is unreadable. Also announces the paywall.
best_line: He is short more silver than physically exists on the exchange.
improve: Naming an individual trader as 'attacker' on position data that the author admits he cannot reconcile (30-40k lots of liquidation vs 1.3m volume) overreaches; label it hypothesis.
The paywall pitch and pricing is placed above the analysis; move to the end.
falsifiable_calls: Bian must eventually buy back ~30,000 lots (April expiry hard deadline)
SHFE-COMEX premium (~14%) normalizes toward 0-5%
When risk-off clears, asymmetry is long silver
return_reason: Clean testable setup (April SHFE expiry, warehouse stocks, premium); check what actually happened to the short and the premium.

title: Long APIs, Short Slides
summary: Pair trade thesis: AI agents multiply usage of consumption-priced infrastructure software (long NET, MDB, DDOG, OKTA...) while destroying labor-arbitrage IT services (short CAP, CTSH, INFY, WIT). Includes balance sheet, vol entry points, and honest risks.
best_line: The shorts get paid per human deployed. The longs get paid per API call.
improve: The basket backtest shows APIs beat slides mostly via 2x higher vol; risk-adjusted edge is small, which undercuts the headline. State sizing (2x short delta) up front.
Long-leg valuation (15-20x revenue) is acknowledged but no entry discipline or exit is given; add stop/thesis-break criteria.
falsifiable_calls: IT services consensus estimates trimmed ~2-3% per quarter over eight quarters (12-24 month trade)
Capgemini highest-conviction short; reporting Feb 13 a potential catalyst
API basket outperforms the body-shop basket as AI adoption rises
return_reason: Explicit 12-24 month trade with named tickers; track the long/short P&L and estimate revisions.

title: Crowded, Confused, Cranky
summary: Market note on a day when bitcoin, silver, CRE and stocks fell together: argues positioning is crowded in AI 'atoms' trades, macro data is contradictory, so cut leverage, hold puts, use credit/bond hedges. Claims early win on Long APIs/Short Slides.
best_line: when everything trades together, the right move is to get smaller until you understand why.
improve: Opening is a laundry list of charts and conflicting indicators; pick the one that decides the cycle question.
'Vol-adjusted 10% alpha in a week' on four trading days is noise; avoid victory-lap framing.
falsifiable_calls: Bond rally could come out of the 3-20yr back end without much front-end move
IG spreads at 50 and HY at 300 look rich; credit is the cheapest protection
Services/IT outsourcers continue to underperform the 'API' basket

title: Don’t F With The Money
summary: Long prosecutorial case against SBF's rehabilitation narrative: FTX was insolvent regardless of the 118% recovery, Alameda hole analysis, and a detailed indictment of his Stanford-professor parents, ending in a two-tier-justice argument.
best_line: When you mess with the money, you don’t get to claim credit when the market recovers after you’re removed.
improve: Off-brand for a macro/markets blog and reads as advocacy; the balance-sheet insolvency section is the valuable piece and could stand alone in a third of the length.
Serious allegations against named private individuals (RICO, money laundering) are stated as fact from civil-suit allegations; distinguish allegations from findings.
falsifiable_calls: Stanford should strip the parents' positions; DOJ should consider RICO
SBF pardon campaign will rely on the 'money good' narrative

title: Blood Transfusion or Blood on the Streets
summary: Bottom-up estimate of Chinese bank losses ($4.4tn base, $7.7tn stress), a $1.1tn recapitalization gap, and an argument that Beijing is extending and pretending, relying on reflexivity; trades are long gold-in-China, short CNH, long KWEB / short FXI.
best_line: The transfusions are real. The bag is too small and the patient is still bleeding.
improve: The first ~1,000 words of philosophy about markets as truth-seeking machines delay the 'short version'; open with the number.
The LGFV 12% base-case loss is acknowledged as below the author's own NPV evidence and 'corrected' to $5-5.5tn only in passing; recompute the headline.
falsifiable_calls: Base-case earn-through takes ~3.4 years (longer, 6-7+, with corrected LGFV losses); stress case 13.5 years
FXI/KWEB ratio falls from ~1.1-1.2 toward 0.75-0.85 in 12-18 months
Gradual RMB depreciation as Beijing eases and eventually prints to recapitalize
return_reason: Quantified, dated trade (FXI/KWEB 12-18 months) and a model that should be updated with new NPL and NIM data.

title: The Death of the New Deal
summary: Argues the postwar social contract is dead (generational wealth transfer, fiscal trap, AI cutting labor share) and proposes taxing inheritance and consumption rather than income and unrealized gains, with a market read-through.
best_line: Tax the selfish stuff. Leave the productive stuff alone.
improve: Evidence section is a barrage of statistics with little sourcing; the 80/20 wage-profit toy model ($82 to $55) is presented as depression math without caveats about capital spending and investment.
Market implications come in the last 150 words as hand-waving; connect each tax scenario to specific positions.
falsifiable_calls: Unrealized-gains tax gaining traction would be massively bearish long-duration equity
Inheritance/consumption route is neutral-to-positive for equities and bearish fixed income
Long gold until the political dimension resolves

title: Where Did All The Stenographers Go?
summary: Historical survey of occupations that died, peak now, or rise with AI, plus a simple three-scenario model of white-collar automation (6-16% unemployment, $0.5-1.5tn income loss) and an optimistic take: long the physical layer, short the paper layer.
best_line: The marginal cost of an analyst approaches zero. The marginal cost of a welder does not.
improve: The scenario model's GDP multiplier (1.5x) and UBI-via-income-tax framing are crude and the dashboard is paywalled; show the assumptions and one chart in the free text.
The 'peaking' list of 9 occupations with AI vulnerability scores is flagged as the author's own estimates; explain the method.
falsifiable_calls: White-collar automation could push unemployment to 6-16% over five years in the modelled scenarios
Long the physical layer (electricians, construction, energy, minerals), short the paper layer

title: All Eyes on Hormuz
summary: Quick weekend note after Iran 'went hot': oil depends on Hormuz status, infrastructure damage and OPEC+ response; highlights vibe-coded dashboards and 24-hour perp markets (Hyperliquid) as early price discovery.
best_line: The democratization of the dashboard is here.
improve: The oil section is generic; the 24-hour-market observation is the novel part and deserved more data (Hyperliquid vs Monday open).
Promises a Monday scorecard of Hyperliquid vs Brent/COMEX gold but no follow-up appears in this chunk.
falsifiable_calls: Hyperliquid weekend prices will roughly match Monday's real-market prints (adoption thesis)
Oil determined by Hormuz, infrastructure damage and OPEC+ response
return_reason: Author set up a clean test (Hyperliquid weekend price vs Monday open) that should be scored.

title: The Regret Trade
summary: Day-after reaction: oil and dollar up, gold, silver, Korean chips and stocks down; interprets this as a scramble-for-liquidity 'regret' trade, recommends long mid-curve oil, and admits an options mishap while traveling.
best_line: “The Dollar is Dead” folks seem awfully quiet today.
improve: Opening list of six moves is strong; the rest meanders into Iran moral/political commentary that the markets view does not need.
Several positioning remarks (TIPS test trade, trimmed copper, Korean stocks) lack sizes or levels.
falsifiable_calls: Long oil in backwardation around the most convex part of the curve or mid-curve
Private credit won't rally even if risk does
Gold and bonds falling in a conflict will reverse (TIPS rolled in size if hit more)

title: Everything is a Bank
summary: Banking is identity; tech companies own identity and are becoming banks; AI agents need crypto rails while humans hold real assets behind KYC gates. Trade: long COIN, CRCL, OKTA (HOOD watch), short KRE.
best_line: Banking is identity. Tech companies own identity. All tech companies are banks.
improve: The Morgan Library anecdote takes ~800 words before the thesis; compress it.
Author admits 'indicative numbers, running without an analyst, AI is not a reliable partner on financial research' yet gives multiples and percent weights; verify figures or flag which are unchecked.
falsifiable_calls: COIN is the highest-conviction long (60% of long side); KRE regional banks a secular short
Stablecoin market $2-4tn by 2030
Identity gate (KYC) remains the control layer for machine finance
return_reason: Concrete pair (COIN/CRCL/OKTA vs KRE) with a stated thesis that can be scored.

title: The Strip vs. The Strait
summary: Argues equities misprice the Hormuz shock because energy stocks price off the forward strip, which is too low as physical infrastructure is destroyed; chains oil to CPI, a trapped Fed, credit spreads and lagged private-credit marks; lists a full hedge book.
best_line: liquid markets reprice first, illiquid markets reprice last, and by the time the illiquid marks catch up it’s already a crisis.
improve: Chart-heavy middle with many captions but few takeaways stated in-line; lead each chart with the one-sentence implication.
'We expect this to continue' calls over a one-week horizon with HYG puts as highest conviction invites a timing problem; state what would make the author wrong.
falsifiable_calls: The oil strip reprices higher (Brent >$100; options see reversion but author disagrees)
The July Fed cut priced by the market disappears if CPI prints hot in May
CDX HY and HYG reprice before private credit marks (BCRED, BKLN)
return_reason: Detailed, dated, option-structured calls (HYG puts, March/April; oil calls 2-5 months) can be graded in weeks.

title: Watch Credit
summary: Argues the next downcycle comes from corporate and private credit: Yale-model 'volatility laundering', Merton-model short convexity, redemption gates and bank markdowns, and an 2001-style analog. Paid section discloses a ~40% NAV credit short book.
best_line: When management holds an all-hands to tell people everything is fine, things are usually not fine.
improve: The opening pajama/VIX anecdote and 'decoder ring' preamble delays the thesis by ~600 words.
The author admits he is not a credit analyst and prefers CDS but expresses via HYG puts and BDC shorts; explain the mismatch and a stop level for a book that is 40% of NAV.
falsifiable_calls: The next down cycle will come from corporate/private credit rather than households (2001, not 2008)
Private credit gating spreads to more vehicles; BDCs below 0.8x NAV
Fed stays pinned by conflict-driven inflation while credit weakens
return_reason: Large, falsifiable credit short book; re-check redemptions, BDC discounts, and HYG levels.

title: Don’t Take the Bait
summary: Sprawling war note: Iran's yuan-for-passage condition, a Rimland-vs-Heartland rebuttal of Dalio's end-of-empire framing (seize Iranian tankers, arm the population), why macro eats every portfolio, and why AI got more powerful rather than smarter. Conclusion: reduce risk.
best_line: The models haven’t gotten 100x smarter in the past quarter but they have gotten 100x more powerful
improve: Four unrelated essays in one post (war strategy, pod-shop risk controls, doomer critique, AI inference) — 5,000 words; the actual portfolio advice ('take down risk') comes last.
Military recommendations (airdrop guns, 10-for-1 tanker seizures) are outside demonstrated expertise and unevidenced; either support or cut.
falsifiable_calls: Oil's back of curve is too cheap and the front is unreliable
Bonds move from pricing easing to slight tightening because of inflation expectations
Precious metals: long-term bullish, short-term pressured (promised update)

title: What the Heck Happened to Gold
summary: Explains a ~10% gold drop in 24 hours (dollar strength, rates, liquidity scramble, broken Dubai-to-Asia pipe, technicals) against a bullish long-term case (bond drawdown, confiscation risk, central bank buying); author cut 80% of the book and plans a systematic series.
best_line: The bear case is right today. The bull case will be right over the next 2-5 years.
improve: The five bear drivers lack magnitudes; rank them, since 'scramble for liquidity' and 'Gulf selling' are admitted as unconfirmed.
The most interesting content (drawdown management, bloat in a 200-name book) is promised for later; give a concrete rule now.
falsifiable_calls: Gold's long-term bull case plays out over 2-5 years despite near-term liquidity pressure
Rebuild positions starting with miners once dust settles
return_reason: Promised systematic gold-signal series and miners rebuild; revisit whether the 2008 analog held.
